1800: The seatbelt sign lit up with a cheerful chime, and forty people ignored it in perfect unison.
1801: You put your phone in airplane mode, and it immediately forgot how to be a phone.
1802: A crew member mimed the safety steps with great care, and you watched, moved, and retained absolutely nothing.
1803: You shuffled down the jet bridge behind forty strangers, all walking at the speed of the slowest one.
1804: The gate agent scanned your pass, it beeped happily, and you felt briefly and officially approved.
1805: You found the little air nozzle above your seat and aimed it at your face like a tiny breeze you controlled.
1806: You hoisted your bag into the overhead bin like a small triumph nobody stopped to applaud.
1807: You lowered your tray table, and it settled at a gentle angle no cup would ever fully trust.
1808: You pressed the little overhead light, and it lit exactly the person beside you, who had not asked for it.
1809: The person ahead stopped to stow a bag, so the whole line paused and quietly admired the ceiling.
1810: Your group was called last, so every good bin space was already claimed by legends before you.
1811: You slid the window shade up for the view, then down, then up again, unable to fully commit.
1812: The drink cart reached your row exactly as you'd finally gotten comfortable, and asked you to choose fast.
1813: You stood near the gate pretending not to hover, hovering, exactly like everyone else pretending too.
1814: A voice invited passengers needing extra time to board first, and you briefly wished that were you.
1815: You wheeled your bag down the jet bridge and it caught every single seam in the floor on the way.
1816: You slipped off your shoes for the long flight, then spent the landing quietly hunting for where they went.
1817: You walked down the aisle scanning row numbers, hoping yours arrived before your confidence ran out.
1818: You opened your passport to that photo of yourself and quietly agreed never to speak of it again.
1819: You found your row at last, dropped into it, and finally let your shoulders down from your ears.
1820: The gate said now boarding, and a hopeful third of the room stood up, none of them in the right group.
1821: You stowed your bag wheels-first, spun it sideways, tried again, and eventually the bin agreed.
1822: The jet bridge angled gently downhill, and you pretended the tug at your suitcase was your own idea.
1823: You pulled the safety card from the seat pocket, studied it seriously, and put it back an expert.
1824: A gate agent asked for volunteers to check their bags on the full flight. Not you. Never you.
1825: You stood in the aisle while someone ahead arranged their coat, their bag, and apparently their whole life.
1826: Your ears filled with a strange pressure, and you worked your jaw around, chewing absolutely nothing.
1827: The final boarding call went out, brisk and slightly stern, and stragglers appeared from everywhere at once.
1828: The gate number on your pass matched the gate above the door, a small miracle you chose to celebrate.
1829: You waited for your group, watching earlier ones board with the calm smugness of the pre-approved.
1830: You finally needed to stand, and of course the cart had parked in your only escape route.
1831: Someone ahead walked past their own row, realized it, and slowly reversed the entire patient line.
1832: The line stalled halfway down the aisle, so you stood holding your bag and studying a stranger's hat.
1833: The engines pushed hard and the seat pressed into your back, politely insisting you sit down and mean it.
1834: Boarding began, so you gathered your bag, your pass, and the last of your dignity, in roughly that order.
1835: You presented your pass to the scanner, it thought about it far too long, then beeped you through.
1836: The overhead bins filled up like a puzzle, and you arrived just in time to hold the very last piece.
1837: A crew member greeted you at the door with a smile aimed at everyone and nobody, and you took it personally.
1838: Your group flashed on the screen and you rose fast, as if speed now would somehow save you time later.
1839: You edged down the aisle sideways, bag held high, apologizing to shoulders you'd never formally met.
